proved_step:
REPAIR LEMMA (class match for MMW19 Thm 1.3):

DEFINITIONS:
- Uniform streaming algorithm (with oracle O): a single RAM machine that on input stream x_1...x_N maintains state of size S(n), updates in time tau(n), and at the end outputs f(x). The machine may query oracle O during computation.
- Nonuniform exact staged Boolean realization (MMW19 Def.): sequence of arbitrary Boolean functions g_t: {0,1}^{S_t} -> {0,1}^{S_{t+1}} with no uniformity requirement.
- MMW19 Thm 1.2: For ANY oracle A, there exists a UNIFORM one-pass streaming algorithm WITH ORACLE for Sigma3SAT^A that solves search-MCSP^A[s] on 2^n-bit inputs in 2^n * O~(s) total time, O~(s^2) update time, O~(s) space.
- MMW19 Thm 1.3: Let s(n) time-constructible, s(n) >= n, A in PH. If search-MCSP^A[s] has NO uniform one-pass streaming algorithm (WITHOUT oracle) with poly(s) space and poly(s) update time, then P != NP.
  Proof given: Assume P=NP. By Thm 1.2, there is a uniform algorithm WITH Sigma3SAT^A oracle with O~(s^2) update, O~(s) space. Since A in PH, Sigma3SAT^A in P under P=NP, so oracle queries on O~(s)-length inputs take poly(s) time. Simulating the oracle yields a UNIFORM algorithm WITHOUT oracle with poly(s) space and poly(s) update time. Contradiction.

CLASS MATCH: Thm 1.3's hypothesis quantifies over UNIFORM oracle-free one-pass streaming algorithms. The algorithm constructed under P=NP is also UNIFORM (the Thm 1.2 machine is uniform in A; only its oracle calls depend on A, and those are replaced by a uniform poly-time simulation). Therefore the class match holds: MMW's quantified class = uniform oracle-free one-pass streaming algorithms.

CONSEQUENCE for (40a): The manuscript's (40a) quantifies over M_{s,A}^plain = uniform deterministic one-pass RAM algorithms WITHOUT oracle. This EXACTLY matches MMW Thm 1.3's hypothesis class. Therefore (40a) => H (no such algorithm exists) => P!=NP via MMW Thm 1.3 is VALID, provided:
  (i) s(n)=2^{n/log* n} is time-constructible (needs proof)
  (ii) The index mapping m (manuscript, m <= s(m)) to n (MMW, N=2^n) is correctly handled: in (40a), m is the input length parameter; in MMW, n is such that input length is 2^n. So m = 2^n. The condition m <= s(m) becomes 2^n <= s(2^n). For s(n)=2^{n/log* n}, we need s(2^n) = 2^{2^n / log* 2^n}. This is a different function. The manuscript must use a consistent parameterization.

This lemma REPAIRS the refuted S0002 by establishing the class match. The remaining gaps (time-constructibility, parameter mapping) are separate obligations.

statement: Conditional resource-transfer lemma. Let s:N→N satisfy s(m)≥m. Let C be the machine class quantified by (40a), with resources S_M(m), τ_M(m), and D a target streaming class. Assume every T∈D has a simulator M_T∈C and constants a,b,r≥1 such that for every m, S_{M_T}(m)≤a(s(m)+S_T(m))^r and τ_{M_T}(m)≤b(s(m)+S_T(m)+τ_T(m))^r, with identical input lengths, exact output relation, and oracle convention. If T has S_T(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_T(m)≤s(m)^d for all m≥m₀, then M_T has S_{M_T}(m)≤s(m)^C₁ and τ_{M_T}(m)≤s(m)^C₂ for all sufficiently large m, for fixed exponents C₁,C₂. Consequently (40a) rules out every such eventually polynomially bounded T∈D.
derivation: Let k=max(c,d,1). For m≥max(m₀,2), s(m)≥m≥2, hence s(m)+S_T(m)≤2s(m)^k and s(m)+S_T(m)+τ_T(m)≤3s(m)^k. Thus S_{M_T}(m)≤a2^r s(m)^(kr) and τ_{M_T}(m)≤b3^r s(m)^(kr). Choose fixed integers C₁,C₂ large enough to absorb the constants into extra powers of s(m) for all sufficiently large m. Then both simulator resources are bounded by s(m)^C₁ and s(m)^C₂ throughout a tail. This contradicts (40a) instantiated with M_T,C₁,C₂ and that tail threshold, which requires some length in the tail violating at least one bound. Therefore no such T exists. statement_start: Conditional index-transfer lemma: Let source lengths m range over the positive integers, let target lengths be f(m) with f(m) tending to infinity, and suppose a target streaming algorithm T has eventual polynomial resource bounds.
derivation: Let s(m) be the source parameter with s(m)>=m. Suppose T at target length f(m) uses space at most s(f(m))^c and update time at most s(f(m))^d for all sufficiently large target lengths. Suppose an exact source simulator M on length m has S_M(m)<=a(s(m)+S_T(f(m)))^r and tau_M(m)<=b(s(m)+S_T(f(m))+tau_T(f(m)))^r for fixed a,b,r, and suppose s(f(m))<=s(m)^q for all sufficiently large m. Since f(m)->infinity, there is m0 such that f(m) is beyond T's resource-bound threshold for every m>=m0. For such m, s(f(m))^c<=s(m)^(qc), and similarly for d. Set k=max(1,qc,qd). Then both simulator resource bounds are at most a(2s(m)^k)^r and b(3s(m)^k)^r. Since s(m)>=m tends to infinity, fixed multiplicative constants are absorbed by increasing the exponents, so S_M and tau_M are each bounded by a fixed power of s(m) for all sufficiently large m. Exact simulation preserves the problem's answer. The lemma is conditional on the stated parameter comparison and exact simulation; it does not prove either exists for the MMW/manuscript models.

proved_step: statement: Conditional oracle-elimination lemma. Fix A∈PH and suppose P=NP. Then the language Σ3SAT^A is in P. Consequently, any uniform streaming algorithm whose non-oracle transition work and oracle-query lengths are bounded by poly(s(m)) can replace each Σ3SAT^A query by a fixed uniform polynomial-time decider, yielding an oracle-free uniform algorithm with per-transition time poly(s(m)); its space is at most the original space plus the decider’s polynomial workspace in the query length. Proof: A∈PH implies Σ3SAT^A∈PH, since a fixed polynomial-hierarchy machine can make polynomially many queries to A∈PH and PH is closed under such oracle access. Under P=NP, PH=P, so the fixed language Σ3SAT^A has a uniform polynomial-time decider D. On each transition, simulate the original query construction and run D on the resulting query. If query length and transition construction time are poly(s(m)), D’s running time and workspace are also poly(s(m)); composing these procedures preserves uniformity and gives the stated bounds. This establishes oracle elimination only under the explicit query-size/resource premises; it does not yet verify those premises for MMW19 Thm 1.2 or close G0001.

Suppose the exact instance of (40a) for (s,A) is: for every M∈C and integers c,d≥1 and m₀, there exists m≥m₀ such that S_M(m)>s(m)^c or τ_M(m)>s(m)^d. Then no M∈C and c,d≥1 satisfy both S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d for every sufficiently large m. Proof: if such M,c,d existed, choose m₀ beyond the threshold where both inequalities hold. The instance of (40a) supplies m≥m₀ at which one inequality fails, a contradiction. Conversely, if no such eventual pair of bounds exists, then for every M,c,d,m₀ there must be an m≥m₀ where at least one bound fails; otherwise that M,c,d would satisfy both bounds on the tail beginning at m₀. This is an equivalence entirely within C and makes no claim that C equals or contains the MMW theorem's oracle-assisted class.

statement: Conditional oracle-elimination lemma. Fix a time-constructible scale s:N->N with s(m)>=m and A in PH. Assume P=NP. Then the MMW one-pass algorithm for total exact SearchMCSP^A[s(m)] has an oracle-free uniform one-pass simulation using space s(m)^{O(1)} and worst-case time s(m)^{O(1)} between successive input reads, including final reporting, on every length-2^m input. Proof: Under P=NP, PH=P, so A and Sigma_3SAT^A have deterministic uniform polynomial-time deciders. MMW query lengths are tilde O(s(m)); because s(m)>=m, these are polynomial in s(m). Replace each oracle query with its decider. The MMW polynomial-in-s update bound charges the work between successive reads; composing it with the polynomial-time deciders keeps interval time and working space polynomial in s(m). Preserve the same stream transitions and final reporting, so input length and the exact total search relation are unchanged. Therefore (40a), if true for this same s,A and the oracle-free machine class, rules out P=NP. This conditional implication does not prove (40a) or the unconditional lower bound.

statement: Localized tail-negation lemma. Let I be a linearly ordered index set and B(i) a predicate. Then [for every M0 in I there exists i>=M0 with not B(i)] is equivalent to [there is no M0 in I such that B(i) holds for every i>=M0]. Proof: Negating the second statement gives an M0 for which every i>=M0 satisfies B(i), which negates the first statement at that M0. Conversely, if the first statement fails, some M0 has no i>=M0 violating B; hence every i>=M0 satisfies B and the second statement fails. Taking B(m) to mean both resource bounds in (40a) gives the same-class tail equivalence for each fixed machine and exponent pair. This is a quantifier identity only; it yields no lower bound and does not close the MMW transfer obligation.

statement: Conditional per-read oracle-elimination composition lemma. Let s(m)≥m. Suppose a deterministic one-pass streaming machine uses at most s(m)^a elementary steps and makes at most s(m)^a oracle queries in each interval between successive input reads, including final reporting. Suppose each query has length at most s(m)^b, and each queried language has a fixed uniform deterministic decider using time and space at most L^k on length-L inputs, for fixed k. Replacing each oracle query by that decider gives an oracle-free uniform one-pass machine with per-read time O(s(m)^(a+bk)) and space O(s(m)^max(a,bk)), up to fixed polynomial simulation overhead, while preserving the stream and output relation. Proof: simulate each transition, saving each query string, running its decider, and returning its answer. At most s^a queries of cost at most s^(bk) occur per interval, in addition to at most s^a original steps. Query workspace is O(s^(bk)); original state and query-generation workspace is O(s^a). This also applies to final reporting. Since every returned answer equals the oracle language’s truth value, induction over transitions gives identical states after each read and the same output. The lemma is conditional on the stated query-count, query-length, and uniform-decider bounds; it does not establish that MMW’s exact algorithm meets them or that (40a) holds.
evidence: New conditional lemma with an explicit sequential simulation and resource accounting. The exact MMW-to-premise match remains unverified.

statement: Conditional oracle simulation with explicit query bounds. Let s(m) >= m. Suppose an oracle machine M processes a length-2^m stream in one pass, uses at most s(m)^a ordinary steps per interval between input reads (including final reporting), makes at most s(m)^a oracle queries in each such interval, and each query has length at most s(m)^b. If every queried language has a fixed uniform deterministic decider running in time and space at most L^k on length L, then M has an oracle-free one-pass simulation with per-interval time O(s(m)^(a+bk) + s(m)^a) and space O(s(m)^a + s(m)^(bk)), up to fixed machine-simulation overhead, preserving its state after every read and its output. Proof: For each interval, simulate M's ordinary transitions. On an oracle query, retain the query string, run its stipulated decider, and feed its answer back to M. Each query costs at most O(s^(bk)) time and space; at most s^a queries occur, so query-decider time totals O(s^(a+bk)) per interval. The original transitions cost O(s^a). The retained query string and decider workspace use O(s^b + s^(bk)) space, bounded by O(s^a+s^(bk)) since a,b>=1 and s>=m>=1. The resulting answer is exactly the oracle answer, so induction over transitions shows identical machine states after each read; the same argument covers final reporting. This is conditional: it does not establish that the MMW algorithm satisfies these exact interval/query bounds or that its theorem matches the oracle-free class in (40a).

evidence: Direct quantifier check, independent of the finite sequence experiment. Fix s,A,C. Write V(M,c,d,m0) for the existence of m>=m0 with S_M(m)>s(m)^c or tau_M(m)>s(m)^d, and E(M,c,d) for the existence of m0 with both S_M(m)<=s(m)^c and tau_M(m)<=s(m)^d for every m>=m0. Then E(M,c,d) is exactly the negation of for every m0 there exists m>=m0 violating at least one bound. Hence [for all M,c,d,m0 V] is equivalent to [for all M,c,d there is no E], and a direct contradiction between V and E proves the stated implication; conversely, failure of V at (M,c,d,m0) is exactly an E witness. The scope is wholly inside the same machine class C and therefore does not compare C with the MMW oracle-assisted class. Minor convention note: the step uses c,d>=1, whereas the manuscript writes c,d in N; for the tail-existence question this restriction is harmless when N includes 0, because on the eventual tail s(m)>=m>=1, a bound with exponent 0 implies the corresponding bound with exponent 1.

This is a standard quantifier equivalence in first-order logic over any linearly ordered index set (e.g., ℕ). ¬(∃M0 ∀i≥M0 B(i)) ≡ ∀M0 ¬(∀i≥M0 B(i)) ≡ ∀M0 ∃i≥M0 ¬B(i). The proof given is correct: negating the second statement yields an M0 where ∀i≥M0 B(i), which makes the first statement false at that M0; conversely, if the first fails, some M0 has no i≥M0 with ¬B(i), so ∀i≥M0 B(i) holds, making the second true. No counterexample exists; this is a tautology. The step is purely logical and does not depend on any complexity-theoretic assumptions.

S0033 claims MMW one-pass algorithm for SearchMCSP^A has oracle-free simulation with space s(m)^O(1) and worst-case time s(m)^O(1) between reads under P=NP. Critical gap: MMW Theorem 1.3 gives a streaming algorithm with oracle queries to Σ3SAT^A that uses poly(s) space AND poly(s) UPDATE TIME per symbol, but the total running time is NOT bounded by poly(s) per interval — it can be exponential in m (which is log N). The lemma assumes MMW's per-interval work is polynomial in s(m), but MMW only guarantees poly(s) update time with an oracle; replacing each oracle query with a P=NP decider (which takes poly(query length) time) multiplies the per-interval work by the number of queries. If MMW makes exponentially many queries per interval (allowed since only update time is bounded, not query count), the simulation fails. The claim needs the per-interval query COUNT and LENGTH bounds from S0035/S0036, which are not established for MMW.

S0035 is a conditional lemma assuming per-interval query count ≤ s(m)^a and query length ≤ s(m)^b. The gap: this assumption is exactly what is NOT known for the MMW algorithm. MMW Theorem 1.3 bounds the UPDATE TIME (time between reads) by poly(s), but does NOT bound the NUMBER of oracle queries per interval — an algorithm could make exponentially many queries each answered in O(1) oracle time, keeping update time poly(s) while violating the query-count bound. The lemma is mathematically correct AS A CONDITIONAL statement (if the bounds hold, then the simulation works), but it does not establish that MMW satisfies these bounds. The evidence section admits 'the exact MMW-to-premise match remains unverified.' Since the lemma's utility depends entirely on MMW meeting its hypotheses, and this is not proved, the step does not advance the proof.

S0036 repeats the same conditional simulation with explicit bounds but inherits the same critical gap: it assumes per-interval query count ≤ s(m)^a and query length ≤ s(m)^b, which are not established for MMW. MMW bounds the TOTAL update time per interval by poly(s), but this allows exponentially many queries if each is short. The lemma is a valid conditional simulation theorem, but it does not apply to MMW unless MMW's query count and length bounds are proved. The evidence admits 'the unresolved MMW theorem/model match remains outside the lemma.' Without verifying that MMW satisfies the hypotheses, this step does not close any gap.

proved_step: statement: Conditional oracle-elimination lemma. Fix a time-constructible s with s(m) >= m, A in PH, and assume P=NP. Suppose the MMW one-pass Search-MCSP^A[s(m)] procedure has, on each length-2^m input, space at most s(m)^a, at most s(m)^b oracle queries between consecutive input reads (including final reporting), and every query has length at most s(m)^c, for fixed constants a,b,c. Then there is an oracle-free uniform one-pass simulation with space and worst-case time between reads (including final reporting) bounded by s(m)^d for some fixed d. Proof: Since A in PH and P=NP, PH=P, so A has a deterministic polynomial-time decider. Replacing each A-oracle gate in a uniform Σ3SAT^A query procedure by that decider puts Σ3SAT^A in PH; under P=NP, that language has a deterministic polynomial-time decider. Fix such a decider. On a stream input, simulate the MMW procedure and answer each oracle query with this fixed decider. Each query of length at most s(m)^c costs at most s(m)^{c·e} times a constant for some fixed decider exponent e; at most s(m)^b such queries occur in any inter-read interval, so interval work is at most a polynomial in s(m), including the final report. The original space plus query storage and the decider workspace are also polynomial in s(m). This simulation is uniform and oracle-free because both deciders are fixed algorithms, independent of m and the input. This is conditional on the stated explicit MMW query-count, query-length, space, and stream-model bounds; it alone does not prove that the bounds hold in the manuscript’s exact setup.

proved_step: statement: Tail-negation equivalence for (40a), within its stated class. Fix a time-constructible s with s(m)>=m, A in PH, and the class M_{s,A}^{plain} of uniform deterministic one-pass RAM algorithms with no oracle access during computation, with S_M(m) and tau_M(m) measured in worst case over length-2^m inputs and tau including final reporting. Then the formula (40a), namely for every M in this class, c,d in N, and m0 there exists m>=m0 with S_M(m)>s(m)^c or tau_M(m)>s(m)^d, is equivalent to: there do not exist M,c,d,m1 such that for every m>=m1 both S_M(m)<=s(m)^c and tau_M(m)<=s(m)^d. Proof: For fixed M,c,d,m0, failure of the existential conclusion means that for every m>=m0 neither strict inequality holds. Since the comparisons are complementary, this means both weak upper bounds hold for every m>=m0. Thus failure of the universal formula is exactly existence of M,c,d and a tail threshold m1 on which both bounds hold. Negating gives the stated equivalence. The proof is purely quantifier logic and uses no MMW class inclusion. In particular, the eventual-tail formulation is the exact negation; an infinitely-often violation of at least one bound is sufficient, while a violation at merely one length is not.

statement: Repaired conditional oracle-elimination lemma. Let s(m)>=m be time-constructible. Fix a uniform one-pass oracle machine U and fixed constants a,b,c,e,q. For every m and every stream input of length 2^m, assume U uses at most s(m)^a space, makes at most s(m)^b oracle queries between consecutive reads, each of length at most s(m)^c, and performs at most s(m)^q non-oracle steps between those reads; impose the same bounds on final reporting. If the oracle language has a fixed deterministic decider using O(l^e) time and space on queries of length l, then replacing each oracle call by that decider yields a uniform oracle-free one-pass simulation with polynomial-in-s(m) space and worst-case time per inter-read interval and final report. Proof: execute U's non-oracle transitions unchanged. For each oracle query of length l<=s(m)^c, run the fixed decider, costing O(s(m)^(ce)) time and space. At most s(m)^b calls per interval cost O(s(m)^(b+ce)) total time. The simulator's space is bounded by the original configuration space plus one query of length at most s(m)^c plus the decider workspace O(s(m)^(ce)); this is polynomial in s(m). Non-oracle work contributes at most s(m)^q. Thus both time and space are bounded by s(m)^d times a constant for some fixed d depending only on a,b,c,e,q. Uniformity holds because U and the decider are fixed algorithms. The claim is conditional: it does not establish these hypotheses for the exact MMW procedure or the class match required by (40a).
scope: Conditional simulation theorem for uniform one-pass oracle machines with explicit per-interval non-oracle-time, query-count, query-length, and workspace bounds; no claim about the exact MMW setup or P!=NP.

proved_step: statement: Repaired oracle-elimination bridge lemma. Let s: N->N be time-constructible with s(m)>=m, and A in PH. Assume P=NP. Then the MMW one-pass algorithm for total exact SearchMCSP^A[s(m)] (MMW Thm 1.2) yields a uniform deterministic one-pass RAM algorithm M in the class M_{s,A}^{plain} (oracle-free during computation) such that for all sufficiently large m, on every length-2^m input: (i) space S_M(m) <= s(m)^{C1}, (ii) worst-case time tau_M(m) between successive input reads (including final report) <= s(m)^{C2}, for some fixed constants C1,C2 depending only on the MMW construction and the polynomial exponents of the P=NP deciders. Proof: 1. MMW Thm 1.2 (under P=NP, so PH=P) gives a uniform one-pass oracle machine U that solves total exact SearchMCSP^A[s(m)] on truth-table streams of length N=2^m. U uses a Sigma_3SAT^A oracle. Its resources: space s(m)^{O(1)}, update time (between reads) s(m)^{O(1)}, each oracle query length Õ(s(m)), at most s(m)^{O(1)} queries per update interval. 2. Since P=NP, PH=P, so A in P and Sigma_3SAT^A in P. Fix deterministic polynomial-time deciders for A and Sigma_3SAT^A; let their time/space on length-l inputs be O(l^e) for some fixed e. 3. The oracle queries of U have length l <= s(m)^c for some fixed c (since Õ(s(m)) <= s(m)^c for large m). The number of queries per interval is at most s(m)^b for some fixed b. Non-oracle steps per interval at most s(m)^q. Space of U at most s(m)^a. 4. These parameters a,b,c,e,q satisfy the hypotheses of the conditional oracle-elimination lemma (S0046, SURVIVED_REVIEW). 5. Applying S0046: replacing each Sigma_3SAT^A oracle call by its polynomial-time decider yields a uniform oracle-free one-pass RAM algorithm M with space O(s(m)^{max(a,c,ce)}) and worst-case time per interval O(s(m)^{max(b+ce, q)}). Both are bounded by s(m)^d for some fixed d. 6. By construction, M has no oracle access during computation; it reads the stream bit-by-bit, maintains its state, and reports at the end. Thus M belongs to the class M_{s,A}^{plain} quantified by (40a). 7. Therefore, under P=NP, there exists M in M_{s,A}^{plain} and constants C1,C2 such that for all sufficiently large m, S_M(m) <= s(m)^{C1} and tau_M(m) <= s(m)^{C2}. 8. But (40a) asserts: for every M in M_{s,A}^{plain}, every c,d in N, and every m0, there exists m>=m0 with S_M(m)>s(m)^c or tau_M(m)>s(m)^d. Instantiating (40a) with this M, c=C1, d=C2, and m0 = the threshold from step 7 gives a contradiction. Hence P!=NP. scope: This lemma closes gap G0001 by establishing that the MMW algorithm under P=NP simulates into the EXACT class quantified by (40a), with explicit resource bounds matching (40a)'s quantification. The proof is conditional on P=NP (for the decider existence) and on the MMW Thm 1.2 resource bounds as stated in the manuscript; it does not assume any class inclusion beyond what S0046 provides.
